picks.title: Longitudinal effects of ambient artificial intelligence scribe use on documentation burden and financial productivity in primary care: a quasi-experimental study
picks.take: A study of ambient AI scribes measures documentation burden and financial productivity. Guess which outcome the budget committee will read first.

picks.title: Takeaways from an evaluation of Google’s diagnostic chatbot, AMIE
picks.take: Google's diagnostic chatbot gets a Lancet evaluation. Next comes the harder test: a patient whose history changes depending on who is asking.

picks.title: Transparency features alone are insufficient for trust calibration in artificial intelligence diagnostic support
picks.take: Showing clinicians how the AI works isn't enough to calibrate their trust. Vendors will respond by making the info icon slightly bigger.

picks.title: Lobbyists and trade groups fight to shape how states regulate medical AI
picks.take: Doctor groups, hospital groups and trade groups are working behind the scenes on state medical AI rules. Nothing says patient safety like a well-attended stakeholder meeting.

picks.title: Reporting completeness of clinical trials evaluating large language model interventions in medicine: systematic review
picks.take: A BMJ systematic review checks how completely trials of LLM interventions are reported. The field raced to deploy these tools, so someone had to read the paperwork.

picks.title: AMA releases governance framework for agentic AI in healthcare
picks.take: The AMA releases a governance framework for agentic AI. Reassuring, since the agents are surely waiting politely for it.

picks.title: Avoiding a 2-Tier AI Ecosystem in Health Care
picks.take: JAMA Health Forum worries about a two-tier AI ecosystem, where well-resourced hospitals get the copilots and everyone else gets a webinar.

picks.title: Why AI-driven payer intelligence is a revenue cycle imperative
picks.take: AI to stop denials before they happen, presumably to be met by AI that issues them. Healthcare's arms race continues, now with better dashboards and the same paperwork.

picks.title: Human-artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time
picks.take: Nature Medicine reports human-AI co-management of epilepsy in real time. A colleague who responds instantly is welcome, though the prior authorization remains stubbornly human.

picks.title: Why AI Isn’t Ready to Tackle Our Convoluted Genomes
picks.take: Wired reports AI lacks the data to decode our dynamic genomes. A rare case of limits being acknowledged before the funding round.
